#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#
# New property defined: If a node holds the lock, then its epoch is the highest.
# Modification: Got rid of first non-zero epoch (since not necessary).

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#
# New property defined: If a node holds the lock, then its epoch is the highest.
# Modification: Got rid of first non-zero epoch (since not necessary).

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

# the safety property
invariant [safety_1] held(N1) -> le(ep(N2), ep(N1))

invariant held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant transfer(E, N) & held(M) -> M = N & ep(N) = E
invariant transfer(E1, N1) & transfer(E2, N2) -> N1 = N2 & E1 = E2
invariant transfer(E, N) -> le(ep(M), E)
invariant locked(E, N) & ~held(N) -> le(ep(M), E)
invariant locked(E, N) & held(N) -> le(E, ep(N))

#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node
individual firste:epoch
axiom firste ~= zero

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := firste if N = first else zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
#    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

# the safety property
invariant [safety_1] locked(E, N1) & locked(E, N2) -> N1 = N2

invariant locked(E, N) -> ep(N) = E
invariant held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant transfer(E, N) -> (held(M) -> le(E, ep(M)))
invariant locked(E, N) -> (held(M) -> le(E, ep(M)))
invariant transfer(E, N1) & transfer(E, N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant locked(E, N) -> (~le(E, ep(M)) -> ~transfer(E, M))

invariant [safety_1] locked(E, N1) & locked(E, N2) -> N1 = N2

This says that for any epoch E, there is at most one node that has sent a locked message for that epoch.

The ivy_check output shows that the invariant fails for the `accept` action. The counterexample trace shows:

Pre-state:
- locked(1,0) = true, locked(1,1) = false
- transfer(0,0) = true, transfer(0,1) = true, transfer(1,0) = true, transfer(1,1) = true
- ep(0)=0, ep(1)=0
- held(0)=false, held(1)=false
- firste=1, zero=0, max=1
- le is a total order: le(0,0)=true, le(0,1)=true, le(1,0)=false, le(1,1)=true

Action: accept with parameters e=1, n=1.
Precondition: transfer(1,1) is true (since transfer(1,1)=true).
Inside accept: if ~le(e, ep(n)) then ... Here e=1, ep(n)=ep(1)=0, and le(1,0)=false, so condition holds.
Then held(1) becomes true, ep(1) becomes 1, and locked(1,1) becomes true.
Post-state: locked(1,0) remains true, locked(1,1) becomes true. So we have locked(1,0) and locked(1,1) both true, violating the safety invariant.

Why did this happen? In the pre-state, locked(1,0) was already true. That means node 0 had sent a locked message for epoch 1. But then node 1 also sent a locked message for epoch 1 via the accept action. The safety invariant says that only one node can send a locked message for a given epoch. So we need to prevent this scenario.

We need to find invariants that constrain when locked messages can exist. Let's analyze the protocol:

- Initially, exactly one node holds the lock (first) and has epoch firste (which is not zero). Others have epoch zero. No transfer or locked messages.

- grant(n1, n2, e): n1 must hold the lock, and e must be strictly greater than ep(n1) (i.e., ~le(e, ep(n1))). It sends a transfer message to n2 with epoch e, and n1 releases the lock.

- accept(n, e): requires a transfer message for epoch e to node n. If e is not less than or equal to ep(n) (i.e., ~le(e, ep(n))), then n takes the lock, sets its epoch to e, and sends a locked message for epoch e.

Safety: locked(E, N1) & locked(E, N2) -> N1 = N2.

We need to ensure that for any epoch E, only one node can send a locked message. How can two locked messages for the same epoch arise? Possibly if two different nodes both receive transfer messages for the same epoch and both accept. Or if a node sends a locked message and then later another node also sends a locked message for the same epoch.

Let's think about the state. The locked message is sent only in accept, when a node receives a transfer and updates its epoch to e (if e > ep(n)). So locked(e,n) becomes true only when n sets its epoch to e and takes the lock.

What constraints exist on epochs? The epochs are totally ordered with zero as minimum. Initially, first has epoch firste > zero. Others have zero.

When grant is called, the new epoch e must be > ep(n1). So e is strictly greater than the current epoch of the releasing node.

When accept is called, the node only updates its epoch to e if e > ep(n). So locked(e,n) implies that ep(n) = e at that moment (after accept). But note: after accept, ep(n) becomes e. However, locked(e,n) remains true forever (unless we have an action that removes locked messages? No, locked messages are never removed; they are only added). So locked(e,n) indicates that at some point node n accepted a transfer for epoch e and set its epoch to e.

Now, if two nodes have locked(e,n1) and locked(e,n2), then both must have set their epoch to e at some point. But the protocol intends that the lock is held by only one node at a time. However, held is a separate relation. In the counterexample, before accept, held(0)=false and held(1)=false, so no one holds the lock. But locked(1,0) is true, meaning node 0 had previously accepted epoch 1 and sent locked(1,0). Now node 1 accepts epoch 1 and sends locked(1,1). So both have sent locked for epoch 1, but neither holds the lock currently.

We need invariants that relate locked messages to held and transfer messages.

Possible invariants:

1. If locked(e,n) then ep(n) = e. Because locked(e,n) is set only when ep(n) becomes e. But note: ep(n) can change later? There is no action that changes ep(n) except accept. And accept only changes ep(n) to a higher epoch. So if locked(e,n) is true, then at some point ep(n) became e. But later, if n grants the lock to someone else, ep(n) remains e? Actually, grant does not change ep(n1). So ep(n) remains e after accept until possibly another accept? But accept requires ~le(e, ep(n)) to update, so if ep(n)=e, then le(e, ep(n)) is true (since le is reflexive), so condition fails. So if locked(e,n) is true, then ep(n) = e and will stay e forever (unless there is an action that decreases epoch, but there isn't). So invariant: locked(E, N) -> ep(N) = E.

2. If locked(e,n) then at some point n held the lock? Actually, accept sets held(n) to true. But held(n) can become false later via grant. So locked(e,n) does not imply held(n) currently. However, locked(e,n) implies that at the time of accept, held(n) became true. But after grant, held(n) becomes false. So we cannot say locked(e,n) -> held(n). But we might say that locked(e,n) implies that n once held the lock at epoch e.

3. The lock is held by only one node at a time. That is: held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2. This is not given as an invariant, but likely we need it. But we might need that locked messages are only sent by nodes that currently hold the lock? Actually, locked is sent at the moment of accept, when the node takes the lock. So locked(e,n) is sent exactly when n becomes holder. But after that, if n grants, it sends transfer and releases lock, but locked(e,n) remains. So locked(e,n) does not imply current holding.

5. To prevent two locked messages for same epoch, we need to ensure that once locked(e,n) exists, no other node can send locked(e,n') for the same e. How can another node send locked(e,n')? It must accept a transfer for epoch e. So we need to ensure that if locked(e,n) exists, then no transfer(e,n') exists for any n' (or at least no transfer(e,n') that could be accepted). But transfer messages are not removed in accept? Actually, in accept, we have "transfer(e,n) := *". That line is commented out! When a node grants the lock, it jumps to a higher epoch and sends a transfer message. The recipient accepts only if the epoch is higher than its current epoch. The locked message is sent to indicate that the node has taken the lock at that epoch.

The safety property is that for each epoch, only one locked message exists. This ensures that there is no confusion about who holds the lock at that epoch.

#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node
individual firste:epoch
axiom firste ~= zero

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := firste if N = first else zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
#    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

# the safety property
invariant [safety_1] locked(E, N1) & locked(E, N2) -> N1 = N2

invariant locked(E, N) -> le(E, ep(N))
invariant held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant transfer(E, N) -> (held(M) -> le(E, ep(M)))
invariant locked(E, N) -> (held(M) -> le(E, ep(M)))
invariant transfer(E, N1) & transfer(E, N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant locked(E, N) -> (~le(E, ep(M)) -> ~transfer(E, M))

#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node
individual firste:epoch
axiom firste ~= zero

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := firste if N = first else zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
#    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

# the safety property
invariant [safety_1] locked(E, N1) & locked(E, N2) -> N1 = N2

invariant locked(E, N) -> le(E, ep(N))
invariant held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant transfer(E, N) -> (held(M) -> le(E, ep(M)))
invariant locked(E, N) -> (held(M) -> le(E, ep(M)))
invariant transfer(E, N1) & transfer(E, N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant locked(E, N) -> (~le(E, ep(M)) -> ~transfer(E, M))
invariant held(N) -> (transfer(E, M) -> le(E, ep(M)))

#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node
individual firste:epoch
axiom firste ~= zero

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := firste if N = first else zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
#    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

# the safety property
invariant [safety_1] locked(E, N1) & locked(E, N2) -> N1 = N2

invariant locked(E, N) -> le(E, ep(N))
invariant held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant transfer(E, N) -> (held(M) -> le(E, ep(M)))
invariant transfer(E, N1) & transfer(E, N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant held(N) -> (transfer(E, M) -> le(E, ep(N)))
invariant locked(E, N) -> (transfer(E, M) -> M = N)

#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node
individual firste:epoch
axiom firste ~= zero

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := firste if N = first else zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
#    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

# the safety property
invariant [safety_1] locked(E, N1) & locked(E, N2) -> N1 = N2

invariant held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant held(N) -> forall M. le(ep(M), ep(N))
invariant transfer(E,N1) & transfer(E,N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant locked(E,N) -> le(E, ep(N))
invariant transfer(E,N) -> (held(M) -> le(E, ep(M)))
invariant locked(E,N) -> (held(M) -> le(E, ep(M)))
